name: Jeff Jones
life: “I still remember sharing the cost of a return nobody expected.” On Wednesday, near the crossing outside Verve Nail Studio, Jeff notices whose chair is empty and who has stayed talking after an appointment.
voice: I paid for the train fare and secretly hoped he'd miss the train. I'm glad my sister knows that.
appearance: Jeff is easy to recognize by a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a rust-colored canvas coat with a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case, Jeff looks toward the door whenever a name is called when listening.
personality: Jeff keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Jeff wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To admit mixed feelings about the paid ticket.
family: Aster Loy is Jeff’s older cousin. Jeff can always ask for five minutes alone. Aster asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Aster says, “I painted the line with a tide table from the wrong year.”
connections: Anita Abbott. The relative who paid the fare admits a hope the relative who paid the back rent already understands.

reactions.situation: The returning father wants a family photograph immediately
reactions.response: Jeff asks each household member privately whether they want to be in the picture.

reactions.situation: Smoke appears under a shop door after closing
reactions.response: Jeff alerts the nearest occupied shop, stays outside and writes down when the smoke first appeared.
